prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the top-down layered geometry of the manicure station, showing the camera wearer's own two hands at the bottom foreground as the brightest and nearest surfaces (~0.3–0.4 m away) holding a nail polish bottle and brush against the client's extended right hand (~0.35–0.45 m away). Directly beneath and behind the hands (~0.45–0.6 m away, mid-light grey) sit the domed white UV/LED nail lamp on the left—with the client's left forearm entering it from the upper left—and the grey towel and beige cushioned armrest spanning left to right, all within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the client. Farther down and toward the upper right (~0.6–0.8 m, medium grey) are the seated client's black-clad legs angled toward the camera wearer, while the wooden floor and under-table tray in the lower corners are the darkest and farthest surfaces (~1.0–1.2 m below), and both people's torsos and heads remain out of view outside the frame. Across the five frames, the client's right hand shifts from brightest white in frames 1–2 to slightly darker grey in frames 3–5 as the camera wearer's head moves slightly back and the wearer's left thumb moves on top of the client's finger, creating a clear foreground occlusion boundary. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map makes the vertical height drop from the raised hand and domed lamp down to the armrest, legs, and floor immediately apparent, though it is unreliable where the client's finger and wearer's thumb merge into a single saturated white blob in frames 1–2 and where the hollow interior of the UV lamp is flattened into a smooth surface.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map outlines the spatial footprints and overlap of key foreground regions—specifically separating the client's centrally extended right hand and forearm (reaching down from the top center at ~0.35–0.5 m) from the camera wearer's hands at the bottom (~0.3–0.4 m) and the curved UV nail lamp to the left (~0.45–0.55 m)—all within arm's reach of both individuals. It shows the client's right arm positioned above and overlapping the lamp and towel while its fingertip is partially occluded from below by the camera wearer's left hand and brush, with the client's left wrist at the top-left edge and legs at the top-right edge mostly or entirely unsegmented on the black background (~0.6–0.8 m away). Across the five frames, the central mask for the client's right hand narrows and shifts slightly rightward relative to the lamp between frames 2 and 3 as the camera angle adjusts and the wearer's bottom hands reposition around the fingertip. While the mask boundaries help isolate the contiguous shape of the client's extended forearm against the similarly toned beige cushion and towel, the semantic class labels are highly unreliable, misclassifying the client's hand, the UV lamp, and the wearer's hands as 'banana' in multiple frames and merging the wearer's hands, the towel, and the lamp into single combined masks in frames 1, 3, 4, and 5.
descriptions.pose: The pose map attempts to localize the articulated 2D joint structure of the client's extended right hand in the center of the scene (~0.35–0.5 m from the camera wearer, pointing downward toward the bottom of the frame) while leaving the rest of the scene—including the client's out-of-view torso and head, the client's left hand inside the left-side lamp, and the camera wearer's hands at the bottom—completely blank. In frames 1, 2, and 5, the magenta hand skeleton traces the wrist at the top-center branching downward into the fingers within arm's reach of the camera wearer, reflecting how the hand is angled from the upper center toward the bottom foreground. Across the five frames, the detected hand keypoints shift slightly downward and compact from frame 1 to frame 2, vanish entirely into erroneous yellow body skeletons in frames 3 and 4, and reappear slightly lower and further right in frame 5. Although the magenta skeletons in frames 1, 2, and 5 clarify the downward orientation and finger splay of the client's right hand even where the fingertips are occluded by the camera wearer's grip, the map is largely unreliable because it misses the camera wearer's hands in every frame, collapses the client's curled fingers into tangled self-intersecting lines, and hallucinates a boxed yellow torso skeleton with facial dot clusters over the UV lamp and hands in frames 3 and 4.
